transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Janene Herbst.
A powerful nor'easter is slamming the Northeast, prompting states of emergency to be declared
in parts of New York and New Jersey where flooding's already taking place.
Steve Castenbaum reports more than 31 million people are under coastal flood warnings and
advisories from the Carolinas to New England.
With wind gusts between 40 and 60 miles per hour, New York Governor Kathy Hochul said the
impact of the storm would be felt most along the coast.
Lots of coastal flooding, perhaps even some erosion that could lead to downed trees, and
that means downed power lines.
A foot or two of water covered low-lying coastal areas of New York during high tide.
The storm was pushing water up into several New Jersey shore towns.
Streets in Surf City looked more like canals.
In Delaware, the storm surge pushed an ocean buoy up into Rehoboth Beach.
The effects of this nor'easter are expected to last until Monday.
For NPR News, I'm Steve Castenbaum in New York.
The White House barred CNN from accompanying President Trump on his trip to watch a college
football game in Tennessee today.
The network was scheduled to provide TV pool coverage for the trip.
This comes just hours after the Trump administration restored access for the network's journalists
to the White House, along with Politico and MSNow.
Empiers David Fochenflick has more.
Right now, all of the other members of the pool are refusing to step in, so CNN is joined
by CBS, ABC, NBC, and Fox News.
So those guys are all stepping away.
So what you have instead are kind of these other outfits which are not part of the pool
and are essentially aligned with the president.
You have RAV, which is Real America's voice, manning this flight to Tennessee today.
And in town, you have Lindell TV.
That's named for Mike Lindell, the My Pillow Guy.
Empiers David Fochenflick reporting.
The Supreme Court has handed a major defeat to Missouri Republicans yesterday in a redistricting
case that could help determine control of Congress.
As Empiers Nina Totenberg reports, the case involves a Republican-friendly map that the
high court had already rejected.
Missouri's secretary of state at the urging of President Trump sought to use a redistricting
plan adopted in 2025, but the state Supreme Court ruled the move unconstitutional, and
the U.S. Supreme Court agreed, twice.
After contrary rulings from two lower federal courts, the high court, for the third time
and with definitive language, told Missouri to cease and desist.
The justices noted that they have repeatedly cautioned against lower courts altering election
rules on the eve of an election.
And in fact, voting in Missouri has already begun.
Nina Totenberg, NPR News, Washington.
You're listening to NPR News.
Harassing or intimidating people coming and going from houses of worship is now illegal
in California.
As Jason Derose reports, Governor Gavin Newsom has signed into law the Safe Worship Zone Act.
The new law establishes a 100-foot zone around the entrances to synagogues, mosques, churches
and other houses of worship.
Inside the zone, it's now illegal to come within eight feet of worshippers for the purpose
of harassment or intimidation.
In the aftermath of the October 7, 2023 attack in Israel, a number of synagogues and mosques
reported congregants being intimidated on their way in and out of worship.
Protesters have also harassed people coming and going from LGBTQ-friendly churches.
Critics of the bill had raised free speech concerns.
An interfaith coalition from across California pushed for the legislation.
Among those leading the campaign were the Jewish Federation of Los Angeles and the Bay
Area's Jewish Community Relations Council.
Jason Derose, NPR News.
Doors of people turned out in Paris for Pope Leo's outdoor Mass today.
The Vatican says more than 600,000 people registered for the Mass.
Leo greeted people as he rode in his Pope Mobile during a parade along the Champs-Élysées,
heading into the Place de la Concorde, where the Mass was held.
This all amid tight security.
It's the first people visit in 18 years and a sign of the Catholic Church's continuing
appeal in a country now officially secular, but once strongly Catholic.
Leo is on a four-day trip to France.
I'm Janine Herbst, NPR News, in Washington.

topics.text: Powerful nor'easter slams Northeast, prompting states of emergency in New York and New Jersey
White House bars CNN from accompanying President Trump to college football game in Tennessee
Supreme Court rejects Missouri Republicans' redistricting plan for third time, upholds state court ruling
California Governor Gavin Newsom signs Safe Worship Zone Act protecting houses of worship
Pope Leo celebrates outdoor Mass in Paris attended by over 600,000 registered people
